newsitem.title: NORWAY: Palestinian hijacker to finish jail term in Norway.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian hijacker to finish jail term in Norway.

text.p: A Palestinian hijacker, sentenced to 12 years in prison by a German court, was transferred on Tuesday to serve the rest of her term in Norway, where her family lives.
Souhaila Andrawes, 44, arrived on a flight from Hamburg to be met by a police escort and a few demonstrators at Oslo's Fornebu airport, news reports said.
Andrawes is the sole survivor of a group of four Palestinians who hijacked a German Lufthansa airliner to Somalia in 1977 and shot the pilot dead.

A Hamburg court convicted Andrawes last November after extraditing her from Norway, where she had been living with her husband and daughter since 1991. The court agreed in June to transfer her back after she fasted for a month.
"Andrawes is weak and frail, but she is happy to be back in Norway," her lawyer, Heidi Bache-Wiig, told the national news agency NTB.
"In a few days she will see her family again," Bache-Wiig said before riding with Andrawes to a women's prison in Oslo.
Some were not happy about her return to Norwegian soil.
"We react strongly against Norway becoming a world prison for terrorists," Reidar Helliesen, leader of the youth league of the right-wing Progress Party, told Norwegian radio at the airport.
Andrawes' group had hijacked the airliner to try to free 11 German Red Army Faction (RAF) left-wing guerrillas from jail, and murdered the pilot when their demands were not met.

A five-day ordeal for the remaining 86 hostages ended when West German commandos stormed the aircraft in the Somali capital, Mogadishu, and killed all the hijackers except Andrawes, who was badly wounded.
She had already been convicted in Somalia and sentenced to 20 years in jail but was freed after a year and went home to Beirut.
